name: The Sumaúma of Tom Jobim

location.address: Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro, near the Aleia Custódio Serrão, Rua Jardim Botânico 1008, Jardim Botânico, Rio de Janeiro

access: Paid entry to the Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro (daily, standard garden ticket)
transport: Jardim Botânico neighbourhood, reachable by bus; roughly 20-25 min from central Rio by car/taxi
verify_notes: Known within the Botanical Garden as 'a árvore de Tom' (Tom's tree): composer/musician Antônio Carlos 'Tom' Jobim (1927-1994) stopped to admire this sumaúma on his morning walks in the garden and drew inspiration from it. A plaque honouring him (an IBAMA tribute calling him 'maestro soberano') was installed at the foot of the tree in January 1995, a year after his death, documented by columnist Antonio Callado in Folha de São Paulo's 'Ilustrada' section, 14 Jan 1995 (cited via Terra). Confirmed alive and standing as recently as Nov 2024, when Ashley Biden (daughter of US President Joe Biden, in Rio for the G20 summit) was photographed posing in front of it during a garden visit, widely reported (Terra, 20 Nov 2024). Height 40.01m per the garden's own 'Trilha das Árvores Gigantes' (Giant Trees Trail), launched Sept 2022 (Agência Brasil), which lists it among the garden's tallest specimens. Species Ceiba pentandra (kapok/sumaúma), native to Latin America, present in Brazil's North, Northeast and Centre-West; the species can live over 100 years and reach up to 70m per general species sources, though no age is documented specifically for this individual, so age is left undocumented rather than estimated from generic species longevity (would be a bridge claim). Location: garden sources place sumaúma specimens along the 'Aleia Custódio Serrão' path; I could not confirm this is the exact same tree as the Tom Jobim specimen from open sources within the time available, so location_precision is approximate (garden-area level, not tree-level pin) and coordinates are the garden's approximate centre. A reader visiting could confirm the plaque's exact spot. No girth/circumference figure found in sources checked.

name: The Giant African Mahogany

location.address: Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro, Rua Jardim Botânico 1008, Jardim Botânico, Rio de Janeiro

access: Paid entry to the Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro (daily, standard garden ticket); this specimen anchors the garden's own guided 'Trilha das Árvores Gigantes' (Giant Trees Trail)
transport: Jardim Botânico neighbourhood, reachable by bus; roughly 20-25 min from central Rio by car/taxi
verify_notes: The tallest tree in the Jardim Botânico's living collection at 49.1m, about the height of a 16-storey building, reported by two independent outlets (Agência Brasil and Diário do Rio) covering the garden's own launch of the 'Trilha das Árvores Gigantes' on 21 September 2022 (Brazil's Tree Day), led by Marcus Nadruz, coordinator of the JBRJ's Living Collection. In the wild Khaya senegalensis (native to West Africa/the Sahel, also called dry-zone or Senegal mahogany) reaches only 30-35m, so this individual is unusually exceptional for its species. No age or girth figure was published in either source; the JBRJ's own detail page for the trail (gov.br/jbrj) required an authenticated login and could not be read, so any additional measurements it may hold (age, girth, exact plot) are unconfirmed. This is one of ten/eleven specimens (sources differ, 'dez' vs the fuller 11-tree list from the same Agência Brasil piece) on the trail, all over 25m tall, including an imperial palm (Roystonea oleracea, 48.1m) as runner-up. Location is garden-area only; exact tree position within the arboretum not confirmed from open sources, so location_precision is approximate.

name: The Figueira Gigante of Tijuca

location.address: Rua Mariz e Barros, 678, in front of the SENAI building, Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro

access: Free, a street tree visible and reachable from the public sidewalk at all times
transport: Tijuca neighbourhood; reachable by metro (Saens Peña or Afonso Pena stations) plus a short walk
verify_notes: A strangler fig (figueira-brava / mata-pau, genus Urostigma) with a short, thick, grooved trunk and sprawling interlaced aerial roots, standing on the public street Rua Mariz e Barros in front of no. 678 (opposite the SENAI building), Tijuca. Individually protected by the state heritage institute INEPAC under decree E 2433, listed 24 October 1968, one of Rio's declared 'imune ao corte' (immune from felling) trees, a legal category distinct from full tombamento used specifically for individual remarkable trees. Described in the source as a 'secular' (centuries-old) specimen; no numeric age, height or girth figure is published, so age_estimate is left as the vague 'over a century' the source itself uses rather than sharpened into a number. Only one source (ipatrimonio.org, a Latin American heritage-listing catalogue that names the decree number directly) could be directly fetched and verified within this pass; a second lead exists (Museu da Pessoa's 'Você Já Escutou a Terra?' digital exhibition, in which environmentalist Maurício Ruiz reportedly discusses this as one of Rio's oldest trees) but that page returned HTTP 403 to both curl and WebFetch and could not be confirmed by direct reading, so it is not counted as a source, only as a corroborating lead. multirio.rio.rj.gov.br, which WebSearch's own summary also associated with this tree via a piece titled 'Árvores integram patrimônio do Rio', refused connection outright (curl exit 7, ECONNREFUSED via WebFetch too) on two separate URL variants, so its content could not be verified either and is not used as a source, per the rule that a search summary is a lead, never a source. No dated recent photo or news mention was found confirming the tree is alive today; the 1968 protection decree and its unchanged listing on the ipatrimonio.org catalogue is the only currency evidence, so this is flagged for a vitality check rather than assumed dead. Address and INEPAC decree number are exact and testable by a reader.

name: The Emperor's Tree of Campo de Santana

location.address: Campo de Santana (Praça da República), Centro, Rio de Janeiro

access: Free, in the public park of Campo de Santana, open daily
transport: Central station (Central do Brasil) or Presidente Vargas metro station, a few minutes' walk
verify_notes: The only catalogued centenary specimen of the Árvore-do-Imperador (Chrysophyllum imperiale, also called guapeba imperial or marmeleiro-do-mato) in Rio, standing in Campo de Santana, the largest green space in central Rio and the site of the 1889 Proclamation of the Republic. The species, native to Rio's Atlantic Forest, is critically endangered and was named for the affection Emperors Dom Pedro I and Dom Pedro II held for it; Dom Pedro II sent seedlings abroad and catalogued specimens now also stand in the botanical gardens of Sydney, Lisbon, Buenos Aires, Brussels and Florence. This tree was planted by French landscaper Auguste François Glaziou (1828-1906), who was brought to Rio in 1858 by Dom Pedro II to run the Imperial Household's parks and gardens department and who also designed the Passeio Público, the Palácio do Catete grounds and Quinta da Boa Vista; Glaziou was tasked with creating Campo de Santana itself in 1871, which converges with the ~150-years-old figure given in the 2023 Diário do Rio piece (implying a planting date in the early-to-mid 1870s), though no source states the planting year for this specific tree in one sentence, so age is kept broad (140-160 years) rather than pinned to 1871 exactly, avoiding a bridge claim. Confirmed alive and under active conservation as of April 2022 (Correio Braziliense/Agência Estado): forestry engineer Sydney Brasil (UFRRJ) climbed the tree, over 12m tall, to install steel cabling supporting two cracked, cavity-weakened limbs, after first flagging the damage in 2019 at the invitation of Flávio Telles, then of the Fundação Parques e Jardins (municipal parks authority) and regional director of the Sociedade Brasileira de Arborização Urbana. Species first described by German naturalist Friedrich von Martius, who arrived in Brazil in 1817. The fruit resembles an abiu (sapote family), pale yellow skin, sweet translucent pulp, historically favoured by both emperors. Height figure (12m+) is the only measurement given; no girth was published in either source checked. Location is Campo de Santana park-level; exact position of the tree within the park's paths was not confirmed from open sources, so location_precision is approximate.

name: The Fig Tree of Rua Faro

location.address: Rua Faro, near no. 80, at the top of the street close to Casa Maternal Mello Mattos, Jardim Botânico, Rio de Janeiro

access: Free, a street tree on the public Rua Faro, visible and reachable at all times
transport: Jardim Botânico neighbourhood; reachable by bus, roughly 20 min from central Rio
verify_notes: Rio's first municipally landmarked tree (o primeiro bem tombado municipal do Rio), by Decreto no. 2.783 of 23 September 1980, after a community campaign that founded the neighbourhood association AMAJB (Associação dos Amigos e Moradores do Jardim Botânico). Planted, per the JB em Folhas account (2023), along the old path to the 17th-century Capela de Nossa Senhora da Cabeça (Rua Faro 80) when the Faro family owned the Chácara da Cabeça in the 19th century. In the late 1970s a construction company (Construtora Marabá) planned to fell or prune it for a building at no. 45; residents, led by lawyer Leonel Kaz, mobilised (first street protest 8 January 1980, over 100 people), the case was covered on the front page of Jornal do Brasil's Caderno B (21 September 1980, 'Uma comunidade decide acreditar na lei e salva a mais velha figueira do Rio'), and the tree was first protected by a federal IBDF (now IBAMA) ordinance, which was then annulled by IBDF itself, before the city's newly formed heritage council stepped in and issued the municipal decree. AGES DISAGREE BETWEEN SOURCES, recorded rather than resolved: JB em Folhas (2023) describes it as over 200 years old ('já está lá há mais de 200 anos'), growing for over 150 years as a neighbourhood landmark before the 1980 fight; AMAJB's own history page, quoting its telling of the story, calls it 'um ser vivo de mais de 350 anos' (a living being of more than 350 years). Both figures are repeated here as given, in the broad band 200-350, rather than picking a winner. Confirmed alive as of the JB em Folhas piece dated 28 September 2023: 'a árvore mais emblemática da região reina imponente no fim da rua Faro, próximo à entrada da Casa Maternal Mello Mattos' (still standing at the top/end of Rua Faro, near the entrance to the Casa Maternal Mello Mattos). A WebSearch summary (not independently fetched, so treated as a lead only) named the species as Ficus tomentella and the address as Rua Faro no. 51; neither of the two directly-read sources states a scientific species, so species is left at genus level (Ficus sp.) pending confirmation, and the page should ask the reader/note the tomentella lead for a future pass to verify against a primary source. No girth or height figure found. Location is street-level rather than tree-level pinned; approximate.

name: Maria Gorda, the Baobab of Paquetá

location.address: Praia dos Tamoios, near the corner of Ladeira do Vicente, Ilha de Paquetá, Rio de Janeiro

access: Free, standing on the public beachfront street of Praia dos Tamoios; reachable at any time
transport: Only reachable by ferry from Praça XV in central Rio: the regular CCR Barcas boat takes about 60-70 minutes each way, with a faster catamaran service running some crossings closer to 30-40 minutes; this is a boat trip, not a short hop, and should be planned as its own outing rather than a quick add-on to a mainland walk
verify_notes: An African baobab on Paquetá Island known locally as 'Maria Gorda' ('Fat Mary'), the main attraction of the island according to Bafafá (2020) and reconfirmed alive and cared for by ABC do ABC in January 2025, which quotes a 64-year-old island resident (Renato Fernandes) saying there have been no recent vandalism incidents and that the tree produced three seedlings that were replanted elsewhere on the island in the past year. Individually listed by the state heritage institute INEPAC (Instituto Estadual do Patrimônio Cultural). It was also one of ten trees on Paquetá municipally landmarked as a group in 1967 (a separate, earlier designation from the individual 1980 Rua Faro tombamento described for rio_005; the two are not in conflict, they are different heritage processes). AGE IS DISPUTED: Bafafá states it was planted in 1627, brought by early colonizers from the African savanna, with a trunk 10m in circumference (recorded as girth_cm 1000). A WebSearch AI summary (not independently fetched, so treated only as a lead, per the rule that a search summary is never a source) separately claimed a specimen 'came from Manaus in 1907' and was named Maria Gorda then; this could not be verified on a page I could read directly (atlasdochao.org returned a Cloudflare JS challenge, 403), so it is recorded as an unconfirmed competing claim rather than trusted. Given the disagreement, age is left broad (120-399 years) rather than asserting either figure. A sign in front of the tree reads (in Portuguese): 'Eternal luck to whoever kisses and respects me, but seven years of bad luck for every unkindness done to me', and residents traditionally kiss or embrace the trunk. Local legend (oral tradition, not documented fact) ties its origin to the death of an enslaved woman, Maria Apolinária, who is said to have vowed to leave a mark of African culture on the island; this is recorded as legend, not as history. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: a different, younger baobab on Paquetá, planted 2013, was deliberately cut by vandals motivated by religious intolerance and later regrew after community effort (referenced in Bafafá and in a separate Diário do Rio headline about a baobab called 'João Gordo'); that is a distinct tree from Maria Gorda and is not this entry. Access is a public beachfront street, free at all times; the only real barrier is the ferry crossing itself, which is honestly stated in transport rather than presented as a quick city stop.
